item.title: Dukes London Returns With a New Chapter in St James’s
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Since 1908, Dukes London has welcomed politicians, cultural figures and travelers to its discreet St James’s address. Now, following a multi-year transformation by Russell Sage Studio, the hotel is preparing to reopen as part of Minor Reserve Collection, marking the brand’s UK debut. The 85-room property will include 13 executive suites and five signature suites inspired by notable figures associated with St James’s. Its familiar frozen martini ritual at Dukes Bar will remain, while a new restaurant developed with The Wolseley Hospitality Group will join the hotel. The Delany Drawing Room, with its collection of 160 whiskies, will also offer afternoon tea and private events alongside its conservatory and secluded garden.

The Curated Take

Dukes is not starting from scratch; its appeal lies in a history and atmosphere that have already earned a place in London’s hospitality story. The challenge of a reopening like this is preserving the rituals people remember while giving the hotel a compelling reason to return. Its combination of heritage, dining and intimate spaces makes that balance worth watching.

item.title: Avani Singapore Brings a Rooftop Social Scene to Tanjong Pagar
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Singapore’s Tanjong Pagar neighborhood will be the setting for Avani’s first hotel in the city-state, in an area where historic shophouses share the streetscape with contemporary commercial towers. The 14-story hotel will offer 200 rooms and suites, along with a green terrace, outdoor pool and AvaniFit gym. Its social center is expected to be SEEN Restaurant & Bar, where skyline views will provide a backdrop for DJ sets and pop-ups. A Lobby Lounge and The Pantry will offer additional spaces for drinks, light bites and convenient meals throughout the day.

The Curated Take

Tanjong Pagar’s mix of heritage architecture and modern city life makes it an interesting base for exploring Singapore. Avani’s emphasis on rooftop dining and social spaces gives the property a personality beyond the traditional city hotel, particularly for travelers who like their stay to be part of the destination’s evening scene.

item.title: Dukes The Palm Dubai Enters a New Era With Colbert Collection
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A familiar Palm West Beach address is preparing for a new identity. Dukes The Palm Dubai Hotel will relaunch as part of Colbert Collection in 2027, with a new name and refreshed look. The beachfront property will retain a substantial resort offering, including 273 hotel rooms and 287 serviced apartments, alongside a private beach, infinity pool and lazy river. Six dining venues, wellness facilities and family-friendly amenities will complete the experience. The relaunch will also mark Colbert Collection’s first presence in Dubai, bringing the collection into one of the region’s most competitive luxury hospitality markets.

The Curated Take

Dubai’s hotel scene is constantly evolving, but a relaunch can be as interesting as a new arrival when it brings a property into a different collection and identity. The combination of hotel rooms, serviced apartments and extensive beachfront amenities gives this address potential appeal for both shorter stays and longer visits.

item.title: The Rasa Resort Samui Brings Colbert Collection to Asia
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Colbert Collection will make its Asian debut on the shores of Koh Samui, with The Rasa Resort Samui set along Chaweng Beach. The adults-only retreat will have 32 rooms, direct beach access and a setting among the palms, approximately 15 minutes by road from Samui International Airport. The resort is also planning a series of updates throughout 2027, including guest rooms with bespoke details celebrating Thai craftsmanship and a transformation of its beachfront restaurant. A new café will add another gathering place, becoming a cocktail bar after dark.

The Curated Take

A smaller adults-only property can offer a different rhythm from the larger resorts that define parts of Koh Samui. The Rasa’s beachside setting and planned emphasis on Thai craftsmanship give it an opportunity to create a more intimate experience, while its restaurant and bar changes add to the appeal beyond the guest room.

item.title: A Historic Mayfair Address Finds New Life as The WestDill
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A Grade II-listed building at one of Mayfair’s most recognizable intersections is set to become a new London hotel. Built by Sir William Curtis Green in 1922, the property at Piccadilly and Albemarle Street will be transformed into The WestDill Mayfair Hotel, joining Minor Hotels’ Colbert Collection. Across six floors, the hotel will have 50 guest rooms and suites, alongside a restaurant and bar. Green Park Underground Station is only a short walk away, placing guests within easy reach of the capital while offering a more intimate alternative to its larger luxury properties.

The Curated Take

The WestDill’s strongest draw is its address and architectural history. In Mayfair, where location is part of the luxury proposition, a relatively small hotel in a distinctive 1920s building offers a different experience from the grand, expansive properties that often define the neighborhood.

item.title: NH Tashkent Signals a New Hotel Arrival in Central Asia
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Tashkent is set to welcome a new international hotel as Minor Hotels and NH Hotels & Resorts make their debut in Central Asia. NH Tashkent will have 151 rooms and a location approximately 10 minutes from the airport, with access to major venues including the UzExpo Center and Palace of International Forums. For travelers interested in the Uzbek capital’s history and everyday life, the hotel is also near two of the city’s notable landmarks: Amir Timur Square and Chorsu Bazaar. Its opening adds another international hospitality presence to a destination attracting attention for its cultural heritage.

The Curated Take

Uzbekistan’s appeal reaches well beyond its role along the historic Silk Road. Tashkent offers a contemporary gateway to the country, alongside markets, architecture and cultural landmarks. The arrival of an established international hotel brand adds another option for travelers beginning or ending a wider journey through Central Asia.

item.title: NH Barcelona Sant Antoni Adds a New Stay Along the City’s Cultural Corridor
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Barcelona’s Avinguda del Paral·lel will welcome a new NH Hotels & Resorts property in early 2027, adding another option for travelers exploring the Catalan capital. The 70-room NH Barcelona Sant Antoni is positioned near Plaça d’Espanya, Montjuïc and Fira Barcelona, giving it a useful connection to both the city’s cultural attractions and its business events calendar. Following a rebrand in January 2027, the hotel will offer a gym, terrace, lobby bar and meeting and event spaces, bringing together the practical comforts expected by leisure and business travelers.

The Curated Take

Not every Barcelona stay needs to be in the heart of the Gothic Quarter or along the waterfront. This location offers a different perspective on the city, with access to Montjuïc and major event venues while remaining connected to Barcelona’s wider cultural landscape.

item.title: Tivoli Mérida Residences Revives a Historic Yucatán Mansion
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On Mérida’s celebrated Paseo Montejo, a restored 1903 mansion will become the heart of a new residential hospitality experience. Tivoli Mérida Residences will introduce 69 branded residences in the Yucatán capital, with the historic Casona 333 serving as the property’s social center. Its original character will frame a collection of guest amenities, including a restaurant, boulangerie, bar and piano lounge, along with a garden and terrace designed for private gatherings. The project brings Tivoli’s Latin American expansion to one of Mexico’s most culturally distinctive cities.

The Curated Take

The appeal here is the balance between the independence of a residence and the atmosphere of a historic hotel. In a city where architecture, food and local culture are central to the experience, placing a restored mansion at the center of the property gives the development a meaningful sense of place.

item.title: Michelin Makes Its Australian Debut in South Australia, Recognizing 77 Restaurants
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The MICHELIN Guide has made its Australian debut with an inaugural selection devoted entirely to South Australia, placing Adelaide and its surrounding wine regions on the international culinary map. Announced October 14, 2026, the guide recognizes 77 restaurants across the state, including Magill Estate Restaurant, which earned Two MICHELIN Stars, and 10 restaurants awarded One Star. Another 16 received Bib Gourmand distinctions, while 50 were included in the MICHELIN Selected category. Among the notable restaurants are Restaurant Aptos, led by American chef Justin James and known for its 16-course tasting experience featuring native Australian ingredients, and Restaurant Botanic, set within Adelaide Botanic Garden. The recognition follows anonymous inspections and evaluates ingredient quality, cooking technique, flavor, culinary personality and consistency.

The Curated Take

A MICHELIN Guide debut can reshape how an international audience sees a destination. For South Australia, the recognition adds a compelling culinary dimension to a region already known for its wines, landscapes and distinctive local produce. It also gives travelers a new way to build an itinerary around Adelaide and the surrounding wine country, connecting memorable dining with the producers, places and regional character behind the food. Importantly, the selection spans fine dining and more accessible restaurants, offering a broader picture of South Australia’s evolving food culture.

item.title: The Wolseley Brings Its London Legacy to New York
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A storied New York clubhouse is preparing for a new chapter, this time as the first hotel from The Wolseley Hotels. Set inside the McKim, Mead & White-designed former Lambs Club on West 44th Street, The Wolseley Hotel New York will bring 77 guest rooms and suites to Midtown, alongside a reimagined wellness center and the brand’s first restaurant in the United States. The Wolseley Members Club will add another dimension to the address, with a private, all-day setting for dining, culture and conversation.

The Curated Take

New York has no shortage of luxury hotels, but a property with a historic gathering-place identity and an established restaurant heritage brings a different proposition. The combination of hotel, dining and private club could make this more than somewhere to stay between city engagements.
